subject: physics
question_text: State the law of equipartition of energy.

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2016 (Q10) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question text itself is sourced from that paper. `appearances` is deliberately left empty — a separate reviewed tagging pass fills it, and a hand-written tag here would be an invented claim. Physics hand-checked against NCERT Class-11 Chapter 13: in thermal equilibrium the energy is shared equally among all degrees of freedom, each carrying ½k_BT per molecule, and a vibrational mode carries k_BT because it holds a kinetic share and a potential share.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. The words thermal equilibrium and degrees of freedom are both checked.
steps.why: A degree of freedom is one independent way a molecule can hold energy — one direction of translation, one axis of rotation, one mode of vibration. Collisions keep passing energy between these ways until every one of them holds the same average share.
common_mistakes: Saying the energy is shared equally among the molecules. It is shared among the degrees of freedom of one molecule.

recall.must_convey: That in thermal equilibrium the energy is shared equally among all the degrees of freedom.
accept: shared equally among the degrees of freedom
equal share for each degree of freedom
reject: half k T per degree of freedom

steps.memory_tip: Equi-partition means equal shares. The shares go to degrees of freedom, not to molecules.

steps.label: Energy per degree of freedom
lines: Each degree of freedom carries the same

lines.text: Energy per degree of freedom = ½k_BT

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The ½ and the k_B must both be written.
steps.why: The half comes from the kinetic-theory result for one direction of translation, ½m⟨v_x²⟩ = ½k_BT. Equipartition gives every other degree of freedom that same average, and a vibrational mode holds two such shares because it stores kinetic energy and potential energy together.
common_mistakes: Writing k_BT instead of ½k_BT for one degree of freedom.
Using the Celsius temperature. T is the absolute temperature in kelvin.

recall.must_convey: That each degree of freedom carries half k B T of energy per molecule.
accept: half k B T per degree of freedom
reject: shared equally among the degrees of freedom

steps.memory_tip: One degree of freedom, one half of k_BT. A vibration is two of those halves.

insider_note: Two marks means the words AND the value — the statement written without ½k_BT gives away the second mark.
